example_reasons.claim-root-cause: All 8 shown failures are demand-forecast-error labeled 'unknown': market-mismatch=#t rows have no forecast-bias, and bias rows (0.065-0.081) fall under the 0.1 cutoff. Broadening the forecast branch to fire on market-signal-mismatch and lowering the bias threshold to 0.06 covers them (~1.33M) without touching the supplier-delay rules.
example_reasons.expedite-response: All 34 alt-supplier rows cost 45000 though observed transfer-days are 2-4 and sister stock is usually present; rows like high/10.0 or high/13.2 would be fine with propose-internal-rebalance at 6000. I route medium/high with inventory-days>=5 to rebalance (fallback still times like alt), keeping the high/<5 alert and alt for tighter stock, so stockouts stay flat while cost drops.

example_reasons.should-arbitrate?: Add the supplied high-confidence gate to the existing conditions. V1 makes 20 false arbitrations among 28 decisions (71.4%) while recall is 1.0; six of eight listed false positives have confidence below 0.7 and would be suppressed, sharply lowering false-arbitration rate while preserving the 0.8 recall requirement.
example_reasons.claim-root-cause: v1’s accuracy is 0.708 with 23 unknowns and 3,161,000 recovered. Broaden that branch to market mismatch OR bias >0.05, preserving supplier-delay precedence and targeting accuracy and recovery.
example_reasons.expedite-response: Change the medium/high branch from alternative-supplier to internal-rebalance. V1's 34 switches cost 1,530,000 and accompany 4 stockouts (2,165,000 total). Rebalance costs 6,000 with sister stock and falls back otherwise; transfer is earlier in the medium/2.8 failure (3 versus 4 days), reducing cost without raising stockouts.
